No advertising to children.
No sponsored answers. No purchase pressure. No sale of children’s information.

01

A learning record for your family.

Our commitment is to use transcripts and learning activity for parent reports and to support a child’s next learning step. No ad targeting, commercial profiling, or use of those records for our marketing or business analytics.

A transcript is the written version of what was said. Activity records show saved questions and activities; they are not a complete record of everything a child learns.

What is scaffolded learning? +

Just enough help for the next step, then room to try. In TJ’s math preview, a child can get a counting clue and another attempt.

Our learning approach uses small steps, useful hints and chances to try again. Learning activity is intended to help choose useful support. Completing an activity does not, by itself, prove understanding or learning gains.

Read the learning philosophy ↗

The native app is in development. These commitments describe the intended limits on data use; its full privacy practices still need verification.

02

What happens to their voice?

Speaking to the native app involves capturing and processing audio, including processing off-device. Our release goal is to discard voice recordings after transcription. Audio handling and provider retention are still being verified.

We cannot yet promise that no service retains audio. Before public release, we need to confirm who processes it, how long it is kept and how deletion works.

On this website: the microphone is a simulation. It plays a prepared example and never records you.

03

The other information an app needs.

The native app can also handle parent account details, child profile settings, device information and technical records needed to run and protect the service. Transcripts and learning activity are personal data too.

Before public release, the app’s privacy notice needs to explain each category, its purpose, who receives it and when it is deleted. Learning reports for parents are distinct from advertising or business analytics.

04

Privacy is a release requirement.

Our release standard includes OpenAI’s under-18 guidance, COPPA and applicable U.S. state privacy laws. Compliance verification is still in progress; this page is not a claim of completed compliance or an endorsement by OpenAI.

OpenAI’s rules for children +

OpenAI’s guidance requires Zero Data Retention before its API processes personal data of children under 13, or below the applicable age of digital consent. Approval and configuration, including the eligibility of the features used, need to be confirmed for TJ.

OpenAI’s under-18 guidance ↗
OpenAI’s data controls ↗
Federal and state privacy protections +

COPPA generally requires covered services to give parents notice and obtain verifiable parental consent before collecting a child’s personal information. It also sets requirements for parent access and deletion, security and retention.

State requirements depend on where the service operates and which laws apply. We need to verify those obligations, including California requirements where applicable, before claiming compliance.

FTC’s COPPA guidance ↗
California privacy guidance ↗
Permission, review and deletion +

Before a public child-facing release, we need verified ways for parents to give the required permission, review their child’s information, withdraw consent and request deletion. Retention periods and deletion across service providers also need verification.

The website’s sample parent controls demonstrate the idea. They do not give consent for the native app or delete a real account.

Current availability ↗
05

This preview records no microphone audio.

This website uses prepared questions, answers, narration, stories and math. No live AI chat, real child profile or child account is involved.

Sample settings and completed demo activities stay in page memory and reset on reload. The demo uses no cookies or browser storage to retain them.

Hosting and tracking +

The website code contains no advertising pixels, analytics scripts, third-party fonts, embedded video players or behavior-tracking code. Narration files are fetched when needed for playback.

Hosting infrastructure can process ordinary request information, including IP addresses, browser information, timestamps and technical logs, to deliver and protect the service. A private preview can also use its hosting platform’s sign-in and privacy practices.

Your motion preference +

Your device’s reduced-motion preference is respected. If you turn motion off here, the choice travels in this site’s page URLs, without browser storage or saving demo activity.

06

A question about privacy?

Contact jrtrustin@gmail.com as an adult. Please leave out children’s recordings, identifying information and sensitive details.

Email links open your email app; they do not add you to a mailing list. If you send a message, your and our email services process it. You can use the same address to ask about that message or request its deletion. This website has no account to delete.

External links have their own privacy policies. We will update this page when practices change and publish app-specific privacy details before a public child-facing release.
